text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA

- Speaker of the Yugoslav parliament Lower House Milomir Minic said the election of Slobodan Milosevic as the new Yugoslav president was of historic importance. Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic said Milosevic's reputation would gain Yugoslavia full recognition by the international community.
- Yugoslavia no longer has direct telephone links with Eastern Slavonian. The region's telephone system has been integrated into the Croatian telecommunications.
- Serbia expects to produce 2.7 million tonnes of wheat this year, which is 1.2 million tonnes more than last year, says the Serbian Chamber of Commerce.
- The Serbian Development Fund has extended 160 million German marks for road repair and construction and 100 million marks for modernisation of railways.

- Yugoslavia has imported raw materials and semi-finished goods to the value of $1.45 million in the first six months which makes up 68.7 percent of the country's total imports, said director of Federal Statistics Office Milovan Zivkovic.
- Montenegrin government replaced director of republican revenue office Dusko Jovanovic believed to be a supporter of Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic.
- Kosovo has the status of an autonomy within Serbia and nothing can be added to or substracted from that, said member of the Socialist Party of Serbia main board Zivorad Igic.
- Secret talks are under way about the participation of Kosovo Albanians in the forthcoming elections in Serbia.
NASA BORBA
- The upcoming Serbian elections will not have international legitimacy if they are boycotted by the opposition, says former Yugoslav prime minister and president of ICN Pharmaceuticals Milan Panic.

- Owners of private petrol stations operating outside the system of the Serbian oil industry NIS asked the Yugoslav foreign trade minister to discuss import quotas. They need to be granted imports of 50,000 tonnes of oil derivatives.

- The opposition Democratic Party said it would boycott elections if the law increasing the number of electoral districts in Serbia from nine to 29 is adopted and would call citizens to demonstrations.

- Trade union of PTT Srbije says that only 20 percent of the 1.6 billion German marks from the sale of the 49 percent stake in Serbia's telecom have come to the country and not 70 percent as Serbian officials claim.
- Serbia is blocking oil bowsers travelling from Montenegro to Serbia, says owner of a Podgorica company.
GRADJANIN

- The list of war criminals for the Hague tribunal was made up by former deputy of the International High Representative Michael Steiner and includes about 60 prominent Bosnian Serbs, a source from the Pale leadership claimed.
DEMOKRATIJA

- Most serious candidates of the Socialist Party of Serbia for Serbian president are former Yugoslav president Zoran Lilic and Serbian parliament speaker Dragan Tomic, according to the paper's source.
BORBA

- Serbia's Commodity Reserve Agency has secured 40 percent of funds needed for purchase of this year's market surpluses of wheat. The remaining two instalments of 30 percent each to be paid by the end of September and October.

- Belgrade City Council to discuss replacement of Belgrade Mayor Zoran Djindjic of the opposition Democratic Party, at the requests of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia and Yugoslav Left, probably at the end of its several-day session.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Retail prices in Yugoslavia in first five months of 1997 rose 3.2 percent, which means inflation of 6.2 percent on an annual level. Present level of prices influenced by heavy burdens on production, primarily interest rates of 10 to 12 percent and half a million workers on compulsory leave.
- Serbian power company Elektroprivreda Srbije asks Serbian Development Fund for 30 million-marks credit for spare parts and equipment. Loan to be repaid with electricity exports.
- Three Vranje companies -- Simko, Jumko and Kostana -- get total 24 million marks worth of credits from Serbian Development Fund for financing export-oriented production.
BLIC
- Around 10,000 people in Yugoslavia infected by AIDS virus.
- Democratic League of Kosova Vice President Fehmi Agani says Alabanians will not vote in Serbian elections.
- Pensions barely cover subsistence; critical years for pensioners 1993 and 1994 when 73,000 people retired and nearly 52,000 pensioners died, says Economics Institute expert.

- There will be no special fund for returning frozen hard currency savings; the state will issue bonds which can be used to buy shares in enterprises, says Mirko Vasiljevic, head of expert team for elaboration of ownership transformation law.
- Highest average wages in Serbia of 2,051 dinars per month in oil and gas industry, lowest of 186 dinars in textile industry.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- President of the Democratic Party of Socialists Milica Pejanovic-Djurisic said the DPS was surprised by the timing of the Yugoslav parliament session at which Slobodan Milosevic was elected Yugosav president. The DPS deputies voted for Milosevic.
- All decisions of the DPS main board have undisputed legality and legitimacy it was said at a news conference.
- Montenegrin Justice minister recognised Milica Pejanovic Djurisic as the new DPS president in line with the decision of the DPS main board.
- The Montenegrin government appointed Goran Rakocevic former culture minister as the prime minister's spokesman.

- Montenegro's January-June trade deficit is $93 million, exports were worth $58 million and imports $151 million. Exports were 47.4 percent higher than the same period last year and imports 11.9 percent higher.
- Average net salary in June in Montenegro was 880 dinars. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
